# cockpit

> cockpit is the local environment coding agents work from on a product of one or many repositories. One reviewed `cockpit.toml` gives Claude Code, Codex CLI and OpenCode the same instructions, skills, permissions and guard hook, including every repository's guides and directory access (`cockpit sync` writes them, `cockpit check` fails on drift). `cockpit session` runs the product's own Compose stack on the live checkouts with a leased port family per checkout and starts the agent inside it. Work orders (objective, scope, criteria with checks) are graded the way the cockpit chooses: by default a fresh read-only agent run (another listed tool when one is available, otherwise the same tool in a new run), or the checks alone, or the agent's own report; the record names which, and a change outside scope fails the grade in every mode. The instructions and guard need only Git and Node.js; the stack needs Docker Compose. Not a sandbox. Pre-1.0, macOS and Linux. The package is not yet published on npm; install it from source as Getting started describes.

## Set cockpit up

- [Getting started](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/b0dea/cockpit/main/docs/getting-started.md): the on-ramp, the safety contract and exact non-interactive commands for an agent setting cockpit up, and the bring-up sequence
- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/b0dea/cockpit/main/README.md): what cockpit is, a sample `cockpit.toml`, the quickstart with its requirements and caveats

## Reference

- [CLI reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/b0dea/cockpit/main/docs/cli-reference.md): every command, flag, exit code and diagnostic
- [Configuration essentials](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/b0dea/cockpit/main/docs/configuration-essentials.md): the `cockpit.toml` tables a typical cockpit sets, with minimal snippets
- [Configuration reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/b0dea/cockpit/main/docs/configuration-reference.md): every `cockpit.toml` field with its type, default and constraints, and a link to the JSON Schema
- [Concepts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/b0dea/cockpit/main/docs/concepts.md): the terms the commands and diagnostics use

## Contributing
